# Sources this skill cites

Each entry gives the exact quote relied on and the date it was checked. If a **Re-check by** date has passed, or the rule is an SBA rule, tell the user it may have changed and to confirm the current version (for SBA rules, the current SOP 50 10 and their lender).

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-change-of-ownership-term

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. B: loan maturities, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A 7(a) acquisition loan amortizes over no more than 10 years (special purpose property aside) and cannot have a balloon.
- **Quote:** "7(a) loans are required to have a stated amortization, loan maturity, and may not have a balloon. 7(a) loans that facilitate a change of ownership must not have an amortization that exceeds 10 years, except as provided below for transactions involving Special Purpose Properties."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-credit-elsewhere

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 1, Para. H: credit not available elsewhere, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The lender must certify that the borrower cannot get the credit on reasonable terms without SBA help.
- **Quote:** "The SBA Lender must certify and indicate that the Applicant does not have the ability to obtain some or all of the requested loan funds on reasonable terms from non-Federal, non-State, or non-local government sources, including from the SBA Lender or Third Party Lender, without SBA assistance."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-diligence-costs

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: financial due diligence costs, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The cost of the valuation and QoE may be passed to the borrower, and what the buyer spends on them can count toward the equity injection.
- **Quote:** "The out-of-pocket costs associated with all financial due diligence reports may be passed on to the borrower. Any funds expended by the Applicant on the report can count toward the equity injection."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-equity-limited-sources

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: limited equity sources, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Limited sources (standby debt, standby seller debt, minority equity investments) may supply no more than half of the required equity.
- **Quote:** "Limited Equity Injection Sources: The following sources, whether individually or in the aggregate, may provide no more than half of the required Equity Injection."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-equity-minimum

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: minimum equity injection, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A buyer making an initial acquisition must inject at least 10% equity, and the lender cannot reduce or waive it.
- **Quote:** "Initial Acquisition: 10%. For Initial Acquisitions, the required equity injection cannot be reduced or eliminated."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-equity-project-cost

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: equity based on total project cost, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The equity injection is measured against total project cost, not just the purchase price.
- **Quote:** "SBA requires equity injections (Applicant contribution) for change of ownership transactions to be based on the total project cost (all costs required to become operational, regardless of the source of funds, except for lines of credit and 504 loans)."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-equity-unlimited-sources

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: unlimited equity sources, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Unborrowed cash (including a gift) and a personal loan repaid from outside the business can supply all of the required equity.
- **Quote:** "Unlimited Equity Injection Sources: Cash that is not borrowed, whether on the business’s balance sheet or from other sources (e.g. gift). Cash that comes from a personal loan to a guarantor where repayment can be demonstrated to come from a source other than the cash flow of the business (the salary paid to the owner by the business does not qualify)."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-personal-guaranty

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A: personal guaranties, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Every individual owning 20% or more of the borrower must give an unlimited full personal guaranty.
- **Quote:** "Any individual who has direct and/or indirect ownership of 20% or more of an Applicant must provide an unlimited full guaranty."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-prepaid-not-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: expenses that are not equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Education, advisory and agent fees do not count as equity.
- **Quote:** "Expenses related to education, advisory services, or fees paid by the Applicant to an Agent are not eligible prepaid expenses and are not considered equity."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-debt-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller debt as equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Seller debt counts as equity for SBA purposes only if it is subordinated and on full standby, with no principal or interest payments for the life of the 7(a) loan.
- **Quote:** "Seller debt that is subordinated to the Lender and on full standby (no payments of principal or interest for the term of the 7(a) loan) may be considered as equity for SBA’s purposes."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26
